original_value: AbstractA novel semi‐active control algorithm is developed and numerically evaluated for the suppression of undesirable structural vibrations. The mechanical energy of the vibrating structure is considered as the primary variable influencing the control action. This intuitive strategy is proposed to realize improved control of structural vibrations. The numerical study conducted reveals that the proposed energy‐based predictive (EBP) algorithm can be implemented on vibration control applications. The energy imparted to the structure is also reduced due to the proposed algorithm. The influence of the parameters of the proposed semi‐active tuned mass damper is studied. Further, the application of the proposed strategy on a realistic structure is numerically demonstrated by implementing the algorithm for the wind response control of a 76‐story benchmark building. The results show that the EBP algorithm is a competitive semi‐active strategy. The robustness of the strategy is also evaluated considering uncertainties in the properties of the benchmark building.

result.paraphrase: A novel semi-active control algorithm is formulated and numerically assessed to suppress undesirable structural vibrations. The vibrating structure’s mechanical energy is treated as the main variable driving the control action, with the aim of achieving better vibration control. The numerical investigation shows that the proposed energy-based predictive (EBP) algorithm is suitable for vibration-control applications and also lowers the energy imparted to the structure. The effects of the parameters of the proposed semi-active tuned mass damper are examined. In addition, the strategy is numerically demonstrated on a realistic structure by applying the algorithm to wind-response control of a 76-story benchmark building. The results indicate that the EBP algorithm is a competitive semi-active strategy, and its robustness is evaluated under uncertainties in the benchmark building’s properties.
